title: 8085 architecture, instruction set and timing
subtitle: Seven registers, five flags, a 16-bit address bus — and a timing diagram that shows exactly when each signal moves.

arch.title: Internal architecture
arch.body: The 8085 has an 8-bit ALU; the accumulator A; general registers B, C, D, E, H, L (usable as 16-bit pairs BC, DE, HL); the 16-bit program counter and stack pointer; an instruction register and decoder; timing and control; and five flags: Sign, Zero, Auxiliary carry, Parity, Carry. The HL pair doubles as memory pointer M.

pins.title: Pins and the multiplexed bus
pins.body: To save pins the low address byte and the data share lines AD0–AD7. During T1 of a machine cycle they carry A0–A7 and the ALE (address latch enable) pulse tells an external 74LS373 latch to capture them; afterwards the same lines carry data. The high byte A8–A15 is on its own pins. Control signals: RD̅, WR̅, IO/M̅, S0, S1. Interrupts: TRAP, RST7.5, RST6.5, RST5.5, INTR.
pins.steps: Why is a latch needed? The lines AD0–AD7 carry the low address only briefly (T1). The latch holds it stable while the lines switch to carrying data.

iset.title: Instruction set groups and formats
iset.body: Data transfer (MOV, MVI, LDA, STA, LXI, LDAX, PUSH, POP), arithmetic (ADD, ADI, SUB, INR, DCR, INX, DAD, DAA), logic (ANA, ORA, XRA, CMP, rotates), branch (JMP, conditional jumps, CALL, RET) and machine control (HLT, NOP, EI, DI). Instructions are 1, 2 or 3 bytes: opcode only; opcode + 8-bit data; opcode + 16-bit address or data.

modes.title: Addressing modes
modes.body: Immediate (MVI B,05H), register (MOV A,B), direct (LDA 2050H), register indirect (MOV A,M — HL points to the byte), and implied (CMA, RAL act on A). Four of the five are visible in the program above.

timing.title: Instruction cycle, machine cycle, T-state
timing.body: A T-state is one clock period. A machine cycle (opcode fetch, memory read/write, I/O read/write) takes 3–6 T-states; an instruction cycle is one to five machine cycles. The opcode fetch is 4 T-states (T1 address out + ALE, T2 RD̅, T3 read, T4 decode). At 3 MHz, T = 1/(3×10⁶) = 0.333 µs, so a 4-T instruction takes 1.33 µs.
timing.steps: LDA 2050H takes 4 machine cycles (opcode fetch, two operand reads, data read). T-states: 4 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 13. At 3 MHz: 13 × 0.333 µs.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• 8085: A, B–L, PC, SP, five flags; 16-bit address, 8-bit data multiplexed with A0–A7.
  • Opcode fetch = 4 T-states; time = T-states / f.
